points.description: States that a static array is initialized only once (not every time the function or block runs). Equivalent wording such as 'initialized a single time' earns the mark.

Links the single initialization to the function call, i.e. it happens when the function is first called (or the array keeps its values between calls). Equivalent wording such as 'initialized once when the function is called' earns the mark.

rubric.notes: Full marks need the student to say a static array is initialized only once and to tie that to the function call (first call, values kept between calls). Partial marks are not given separately; a student who gives only the single-initialization idea gets P1 (3/5). No marks are given for a vague answer about static arrays being different without saying how initialization differs. The question asks for a difference, so a clear contrast with non-static arrays is acceptable but not required because the model answer only describes the static case.
